title: After a painful skin injury, a patient has an exaggerated response to later stimulation. In a model of synaptic sensitization, serotonin activates a cAMP pathw…
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: After a painful skin injury, a patient has an exaggerated response to later stimulation. In a model of synaptic sensitization, serotonin activates a cAMP pathway that reduces K⁺ conductance in a presynaptic sensory terminal. Which additional finding would most directly explain the larger postsynaptic response?
options: Shorter presynaptic action potentials with reduced Ca²⁺ entry
Larger individual action potentials caused by temporal summation within the axon
Increased K⁺ efflux that accelerates depolarization
Prolonged presynaptic depolarization that increases Ca²⁺ entry and transmitter release
Conversion of postsynaptic graded potentials into signals that no longer need threshold
Reduced transmitter release with increased transmitter destruction
body.explanation: Less outward K⁺ current slows repolarization; the longer depolarization lets more Ca²⁺ in, so more transmitter is released. Action potentials do not summate in amplitude.

title: Compared with chemical synapses, electrical synapses:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Compared with chemical synapses, electrical synapses:
options: Need neurotransmitters released from vesicles and are slower, passing signals in one direction only
Pass current directly through gap junctions, quickly and often in both directions
body.explanation: Chemical synapses are one-way and slower but can amplify and be modulated.

title: A single presynaptic neuron fires three action potentials in rapid succession at the same synapse, and the postsynaptic neuron reaches threshold. This is an ex…
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A single presynaptic neuron fires three action potentials in rapid succession at the same synapse, and the postsynaptic neuron reaches threshold. This is an example of
body.explanation: Temporal: one neuron, repeated firing. Spatial: several neurons at the same time at different places. Each PSP is only about 10 mV, so summation is needed.

title: CSF is produced mainly by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: CSF is produced mainly by:
body.explanation: It is reabsorbed by the arachnoid granulations into the superior sagittal sinus.

title: A stimulus depolarizes a neuron's axon hillock from -70 mV to -62 mV. What happens?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A stimulus depolarizes a neuron's axon hillock from -70 mV to -62 mV. What happens?
options: A graded potential occurs but no action potential fires
body.explanation: Threshold is about -50 to -55 mV. Below it the change stays a local graded potential; action potentials are all-or-none.

title: Thanks to the buoyancy provided by cerebrospinal fluid, the effective weight of a 1400 g brain is reduced to about
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Thanks to the buoyancy provided by cerebrospinal fluid, the effective weight of a 1400 g brain is reduced to about
body.explanation: Buoyancy is one of the four functions of CSF, with protection, excretion of waste and acting as an endocrine medium.

title: Sympathetic stimulation causes:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Sympathetic stimulation causes:
options: Pupil dilation and reduced gut motility
Pupil constriction, copious saliva and increased gut motility
body.explanation: Parasympathetic: miosis, copious saliva, more gut motility.

title: You no longer feel your watch on your wrist a few minutes after putting it on. This is mainly due to
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: You no longer feel your watch on your wrist a few minutes after putting it on. This is mainly due to
options: Rapid adaptation of phasic touch receptors
body.explanation: Phasic receptors (touch, temperature, smell) signal change and adapt rapidly; tonic receptors (proprioceptors) adapt slowly.

title: The main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain is
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The main inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain is
body.explanation: Glutamate is the main excitatory transmitter; GABA (and glycine) are inhibitory.

title: At all autonomic ganglia, the neurotransmitter and receptor are
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: At all autonomic ganglia, the neurotransmitter and receptor are
body.explanation: ACh acts on nicotinic receptors at all autonomic ganglia and on muscarinic receptors at parasympathetic terminals.

title: A neurologist places a vibrating tuning fork on a patient's fingertip. The receptor mainly responsible for detecting the vibration is the
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A neurologist places a vibrating tuning fork on a patient's fingertip. The receptor mainly responsible for detecting the vibration is the
body.explanation: Pacinian corpuscles are rapidly adapting vibration detectors. Merkel: form and texture; Meissner: motion and grip; Ruffini: skin stretch.

title: Acetylcholine excites skeletal muscle but slows the heart. This is because
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Acetylcholine excites skeletal muscle but slows the heart. This is because
options: ACh is broken down faster in the heart
ACh acts on the heart only through noradrenaline
The effect depends on the receptor type (nicotinic or muscarinic)
Different neurons release different forms of ACh
Cardiac muscle has no ACh receptors
body.explanation: Nicotinic receptors at the NMJ are excitatory; muscarinic receptors in the heart are inhibitory.

title: During the stretch reflex, the antagonist muscle:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: During the stretch reflex, the antagonist muscle:
body.explanation: An inhibitory interneuron inhibits the antagonist.

title: An action potential normally travels in only one direction along the axon because
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: An action potential normally travels in only one direction along the axon because
options: The Na⁺/K⁺ pump is located only at the terminal
The axon has no Na⁺ channels near the cell body
Na⁺ channels behind it are inactivated
K⁺ channels ahead of it are closed
body.explanation: Inactivated Na⁺ channels cannot reopen straight away, so the patch behind the action potential cannot fire again.

title: Which statement about the sliding filament mechanism is correct?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which statement about the sliding filament mechanism is correct?
options: The H zone narrows while the A band stays the same
body.explanation: Filaments keep their length and slide; the I band and H zone shorten.

title: A patient has disruption of the ossicular chain after trauma. Which function is most directly impaired?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A patient has disruption of the ossicular chain after trauma. Which function is most directly impaired?
options: Conversion of stereocilia movement into a receptor potential
Amplification of pressure transmitted from air to cochlear fluid
Encoding of high-frequency sounds at the base of the cochlea
Release of glutamate from inner hair cells
Transmission of auditory information through the cochlear nerve
body.explanation: The ossicles (lever) and the tympanic membrane to oval window area ratio raise pressure about 20-fold: impedance matching from air to fluid.

title: A man touches a hot pan. He first feels a sharp, well-localised pain, followed a second later by a dull burning pain. The burning second pain is carried by
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A man touches a hot pan. He first feels a sharp, well-localised pain, followed a second later by a dull burning pain. The burning second pain is carried by
body.explanation: First (sharp) pain travels in A-delta fibres; second (burning) pain in slow unmyelinated C fibres.

title: A drug blocks voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels in the presynaptic terminal. The action potential still reaches the terminal normally. What is the most likely result?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A drug blocks voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels in the presynaptic terminal. The action potential still reaches the terminal normally. What is the most likely result?
options: The action potential can no longer propagate along the axon
body.explanation: Ca²⁺ entry is the link between the electrical and the chemical step: it triggers exocytosis of synaptic vesicles.

title: The main excitatory neurotransmitter of the CNS is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The main excitatory neurotransmitter of the CNS is:
body.explanation: GABA (brain) and glycine (spinal cord) are the main inhibitory ones.

title: Which substance sensitises nociceptors without exciting them directly?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which substance sensitises nociceptors without exciting them directly?
body.explanation: Prostaglandins and substance P sensitise; NSAIDs block prostaglandin synthesis.

title: A blind student reads Braille with her fingertips. Detecting the shape and texture of the dots relies mostly on
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A blind student reads Braille with her fingertips. Detecting the shape and texture of the dots relies mostly on
body.explanation: Merkel discs are slowly adapting and detect form and texture; they make up about 25% of hand receptors.

title: After leaving the fourth ventricle, cerebrospinal fluid reaches the subarachnoid space mainly through
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: After leaving the fourth ventricle, cerebrospinal fluid reaches the subarachnoid space mainly through
options: The choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle
body.explanation: CSF flow: lateral ventricles → foramen of Monro → third ventricle → cerebral aqueduct → fourth ventricle → foramen of Magendie → subarachnoid space → arachnoid granulations → superior sagittal sinus.

title: A student holds a heavy suitcase still with the elbow flexed at 90°. The biceps develops tension without changing length. This is
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A student holds a heavy suitcase still with the elbow flexed at 90°. The biceps develops tension without changing length. This is
body.explanation: Isometric: myosin heads generate tension but the thin filaments cannot slide because the load is too great. Isotonic: the muscle shortens and the load moves.

title: The equilibrium potential of Na⁺ in a typical neuron is approximately
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The equilibrium potential of Na⁺ in a typical neuron is approximately
body.explanation: ENa about +60 mV; EK about -90 mV; rest -70 mV; threshold -50 to -55 mV.

title: The resting membrane potential of a typical neuron is about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The resting membrane potential of a typical neuron is about:
body.explanation: Action potentials overshoot to about +30 mV.

title: An unvaccinated farmer develops lockjaw and painful muscle spasms after a deep wound. Tetanus toxin causes these signs by
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: An unvaccinated farmer develops lockjaw and painful muscle spasms after a deep wound. Tetanus toxin causes these signs by
options: Blocking presynaptic Ca²⁺ channels at the NMJ
Preventing GABA release from inhibitory neurons
Blocking nicotinic receptors at the end plate
body.explanation: Loss of inhibition leaves excitation unopposed.

title: Which sympathetic target receives postganglionic fibres that release acetylcholine?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which sympathetic target receives postganglionic fibres that release acetylcholine?
options: The dilator muscle of the pupil
body.explanation: Sweat glands are the cholinergic sympathetic exception. Renal vessels receive dopamine; the adrenal medulla is reached by preganglionic fibres.

title: Neurotransmitter release at the axon terminal is triggered by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Neurotransmitter release at the axon terminal is triggered by:
options: Na⁺ entry alone, through voltage-gated Na⁺ channels
Ca²⁺ entry through voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels
body.explanation: Ca²⁺ triggers vesicle fusion (exocytosis).

title: Which event directly triggers the exocytosis of synaptic vesicles?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which event directly triggers the exocytosis of synaptic vesicles?
options: Entry of Ca²⁺ into the presynaptic terminal
Binding of transmitter to postsynaptic receptors
Entry of Cl⁻ into the terminal
body.explanation: Six events: action potential, Ca²⁺ entry, release, receptor binding, ions enter, graded potential.

title: The depolarisation phase of the action potential is due to:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The depolarisation phase of the action potential is due to:
body.explanation: Repolarisation = K⁺ efflux; Na⁺ channels then inactivate.

title: The dihydropyridine (DHP) receptor of skeletal muscle is
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The dihydropyridine (DHP) receptor of skeletal muscle is
options: A voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channel in the T-tubule membrane
A Ca²⁺ release channel of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
The acetylcholine receptor of the end plate
The Ca²⁺ pump that refills the sarcoplasmic reticulum
body.explanation: The DHP receptor gates the ryanodine receptor (SR release channel); SERCA pumps Ca²⁺ back.

title: A triad in skeletal muscle is made of
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A triad in skeletal muscle is made of
options: Two T-tubules and one terminal cisterna
One Z disc and two M lines
One T-tubule and two terminal cisternae of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
body.explanation: The T-tubule carries the action potential; the terminal cisternae store and release Ca²⁺.

title: A 30-year-old man has a focal injury of the left anterolateral column of the thoracic spinal cord. Pain and temperature sensation are reduced on the right side…
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A 30-year-old man has a focal injury of the left anterolateral column of the thoracic spinal cord. Pain and temperature sensation are reduced on the right side below the injury, while vibration and joint-position sense are intact. Which neuronal arrangement best explains this pattern?
options: Primary pain afferents cross in the spinal cord and ascend in the posterior columns
Second-order pain neurons ascend ipsilaterally and cross only after reaching the thalamus
Primary pain afferents ascend directly to the cortex without an intervening synapse
Second-order neurons carrying vibration cross within the spinal cord and ascend anterolaterally
Pain and vibration are carried by the same spinal pathway but activate different cortical receptors
Primary pain afferents synapse in the dorsal horn, and second-order axons cross before ascending contralaterally
body.explanation: Pain afferents synapse in the dorsal horn; second-order axons cross in the cord and ascend in the opposite anterolateral column. Vibration uses the posterior columns, which are spared.

title: A child has a tumour that blocks the cerebral aqueduct. Which ventricles are expected to dilate?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A child has a tumour that blocks the cerebral aqueduct. Which ventricles are expected to dilate?
options: The lateral ventricles and the third ventricle
body.explanation: CSF made upstream of the aqueduct cannot leave, so the lateral and third ventricles dilate; the fourth is downstream.

title: Habituation to a repeated harmless stimulus results mainly from
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Habituation to a repeated harmless stimulus results mainly from
options: Faster conduction in the afferent axon
Release of serotonin onto the sensory terminal
Reduced activity of presynaptic voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels
Blocking of K⁺ channels by a cAMP cascade
body.explanation: Habituation depresses synaptic activity. The K⁺ channel block through serotonin and cAMP is the mechanism of sensitization.

title: After six months of strength training, a weightlifter's biceps is much larger. This is mainly due to
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: After six months of strength training, a weightlifter's biceps is much larger. This is mainly due to
options: An increase in the number of motor neurons
Conversion of smooth muscle into skeletal muscle
An increase in the number of fibres (hyperplasia)
Fusion of new myoblasts into extra fibres
body.explanation: The number of skeletal muscle fibres is fixed at birth.

title: Action potentials are normally initiated at:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Action potentials are normally initiated at:
options: The dendrites, where most synapses are
body.explanation: It has the highest density of voltage-gated Na⁺ channels.

title: The receptor of the stretch reflex is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The receptor of the stretch reflex is:
body.explanation: Golgi tendon organs sense tension (Ib fibres) and cause the inverse myotatic reflex.

title: Which protein spans half a sarcomere, anchors thick filaments to the Z disc and gives the sarcomere elasticity?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which protein spans half a sarcomere, anchors thick filaments to the Z disc and gives the sarcomere elasticity?
body.explanation: Titin is structural and elastic; nebulin is non-elastic along actin; tropomyosin and troponin are regulatory.

title: A patient has a hemisection of the right half of the spinal cord at T10. Which finding is expected below the lesion?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A patient has a hemisection of the right half of the spinal cord at T10. Which finding is expected below the lesion?
options: Loss of vibration sense on the left side
Loss of pain and temperature on the right side
Loss of all sensation on both sides
Loss of pain and temperature on the left side
Loss of fine touch on the left side
body.explanation: Pain and temperature fibres cross in the spinal cord, so they are lost on the opposite side. Fine touch, vibration and proprioception cross in the medulla, so they are lost on the same side.

title: The gate control theory states that pain transmission in the dorsal horn can be reduced by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The gate control theory states that pain transmission in the dorsal horn can be reduced by:
options: Activity in large Aβ touch fibres
More activity in thin unmyelinated C fibres
body.explanation: Rubbing a painful area activates inhibitory interneurons.

title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) act by
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) act by
options: Keeping serotonin longer in the synaptic cleft
body.explanation: Blocking reuptake prolongs the transmitter's action, the lecture's example of a drug acting on removal.

title: Spatial summation means:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Spatial summation means:
options: One synapse firing rapidly, so that its successive inputs add up over time
Inputs from several synapses arriving at the same time add up
Signals travelling back up the axon
body.explanation: Temporal summation = repeated firing of one synapse.

title: The myotatic (stretch) reflex is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The myotatic (stretch) reflex is:
options: Monosynaptic: Ia afferent to alpha motor neuron
Polysynaptic, through interneurons in the dorsal horn
body.explanation: The muscle spindle senses stretch.

title: Compared with chemical synapses, electrical synapses
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Compared with chemical synapses, electrical synapses
options: Can amplify and be modulated by drugs
Pass current through gap junctions with almost no delay
body.explanation: Electrical synapses are fast and can conduct both ways. Chemical synapses are one-way, have a synaptic delay and can be modulated.

title: Compared with direct (channel-linked) receptors, receptors that act through G proteins and cAMP produce responses that are
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Compared with direct (channel-linked) receptors, receptors that act through G proteins and cAMP produce responses that are
body.explanation: Indirect receptors (biogenic amines, peptides, gases) give slow synapses; direct receptors (ACh, amino acids) give fast synapses.

title: Two-point discrimination is much better on the fingertip than on the lower leg because the fingertip has
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Two-point discrimination is much better on the fingertip than on the lower leg because the fingertip has
body.explanation: Small, dense receptive fields plus lateral inhibition sharpen localisation; the cortical area matches the sensitivity.

title: The adrenal medulla differs from other sympathetic targets because it
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The adrenal medulla differs from other sympathetic targets because it
options: Is supplied directly by preganglionic fibres
Releases noradrenaline and adrenaline in a 1:4 ratio
body.explanation: The adrenal medulla acts like a sympathetic ganglion and releases adrenaline and noradrenaline about 4:1.

title: In a typical multipolar neuron, the action potential is initiated at the
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In a typical multipolar neuron, the action potential is initiated at the
options: Node of Ranvier nearest the terminal
body.explanation: Trigger zone = axon hillock. Input zone = dendrites and soma; output zone = axon terminals.

title: A sound wave displaces the basilar membrane and bends hair-cell stereocilia toward their excitatory direction. Which event occurs next?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A sound wave displaces the basilar membrane and bends hair-cell stereocilia toward their excitatory direction. Which event occurs next?
options: Ca²⁺ efflux from the hair cell
body.explanation: K⁺-rich endolymph enters through mechanically gated channels and depolarizes the cell; voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels then open and glutamate is released.

title: The correct CSF pathway is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The correct CSF pathway is:
options: Lateral ventricles → fourth ventricle → cerebral aqueduct → third ventricle → foramen of Monro → subarachnoid space
Lateral ventricles → foramen of Monro → third ventricle → cerebral aqueduct → fourth ventricle → subarachnoid space
Subarachnoid space → choroid plexus → lateral ventricles
Lateral ventricles → fourth ventricle → third ventricle
body.explanation: It leaves the fourth ventricle through the foramina of Magendie (and Luschka).

title: Fast pain is carried by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Fast pain is carried by:
body.explanation: A-delta: sharp, well localised; C fibres: slow, burning pain.

title: A muscle tissue is striated, involuntary and its cells are linked by gap junctions. It is
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A muscle tissue is striated, involuntary and its cells are linked by gap junctions. It is
body.explanation: Smooth muscle is not striated; skeletal muscle is voluntary and has no gap junctions. Cardiac cells connect through intercalated discs.

title: A patient receives a drug that stimulates muscarinic receptors. Which effect is expected?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A patient receives a drug that stimulates muscarinic receptors. Which effect is expected?
body.explanation: Muscarinic receptors mediate parasympathetic effects: miosis, copious saliva, bronchoconstriction, slower heart, more gut motility.

title: Mature neurons cannot divide because they lack
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Mature neurons cannot divide because they lack
body.explanation: Neurons have a nucleus, Nissl granules, Golgi and mitochondria, but no centrosome.

title: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, which region keeps a constant length?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, which region keeps a constant length?
body.explanation: The A band equals the thick filament length, and filaments do not change length. The I band and H zone shorten.

title: The nicotinic acetylcholine receptor of the motor end plate is an example of a
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The nicotinic acetylcholine receptor of the motor end plate is an example of a
body.explanation: It opens when a chemical (ACh) binds.

title: Brisk (exaggerated) tendon reflexes suggest:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Brisk (exaggerated) tendon reflexes suggest:
options: An upper motor neuron lesion above the arc
A peripheral neuropathy affecting the sensory fibres of the arc
A lesion of the reflex arc
body.explanation: Weak or absent reflexes point to the arc itself.

title: A patient with kidney failure has a high extracellular K⁺ concentration. What happens to the resting membrane potential of his neurons?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A patient with kidney failure has a high extracellular K⁺ concentration. What happens to the resting membrane potential of his neurons?
options: It becomes equal to the Na⁺ equilibrium potential
body.explanation: The resting potential sits near EK. Raising outside K⁺ reduces the gradient driving K⁺ out, so EK and the resting potential become less negative.

title: Graded potentials:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Graded potentials:
options: Vary in size with the stimulus and fade with distance
Travel without decrement along the axon, like action potentials
body.explanation: Action potentials are all-or-none and conducted without decrement.

title: In smooth muscle, the Ca²⁺-binding protein that starts contraction is
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: In smooth muscle, the Ca²⁺-binding protein that starts contraction is
body.explanation: Skeletal and cardiac muscle use troponin; smooth muscle uses calmodulin.

title: The dorsal (posterior) column pathway carries
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The dorsal (posterior) column pathway carries
options: Visceral pain from the abdominal organs
Automatic postural tone from the vestibular nuclei
Voluntary motor commands to distal limbs
Discriminative touch, vibration and conscious proprioception
body.explanation: Pain, temperature and crude touch travel in the anterolateral (spinothalamic) system.

title: Inactivation of voltage-gated Na⁺ channels explains:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Inactivation of voltage-gated Na⁺ channels explains:
body.explanation: A new action potential cannot fire until the channels recover.

title: Allodynia is:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Allodynia is:
options: Pain from a normally harmless stimulus
An exaggerated response to a painful stimulus
body.explanation: Hyperalgesia = exaggerated response to a noxious stimulus.

title: Pain receptors (nociceptors) are:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Pain receptors (nociceptors) are:
options: Free nerve endings that adapt very little
body.explanation: Little adaptation keeps the warning going.

title: Myelin in the central nervous system is formed by
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Myelin in the central nervous system is formed by
body.explanation: Oligodendrocytes in the CNS, Schwann cells in the PNS.

title: A patient has damage to the chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve. Which sensory function is most directly affected?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A patient has damage to the chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve. Which sensory function is most directly affected?
options: Taste from the posterior one-third of the tongue
Taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue
Taste from the pharynx and epiglottis
Texture and temperature of food sensed by the trigeminal nerve
body.explanation: Chorda tympani (VII): anterior 2/3. IX: posterior 1/3. X: pharynx and epiglottis. V: texture and temperature.

title: The afterhyperpolarization at the end of an action potential is mainly caused by
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: The afterhyperpolarization at the end of an action potential is mainly caused by
options: Entry of Ca²⁺ through ligand-gated channels
Slow closure of voltage-gated K⁺ channels
Activation of the Na⁺/K⁺ pump alone
body.explanation: K⁺ channels open and close slowly, so K⁺ keeps leaving briefly after the membrane is back at rest.

title: Which statement correctly describes a graded potential?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Which statement correctly describes a graded potential?
options: Its amplitude is proportional to the stimulus and it decreases with distance
It travels long distances without decrement
It occurs only in membranes with voltage-gated channels
body.explanation: Graded potentials are local and can be excitatory or inhibitory; action potentials are all-or-none and travel without decrement.

title: Myelin in the CNS is made by:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Myelin in the CNS is made by:
options: Schwann cells, each wrapping one internode
body.explanation: Schwann cells myelinate peripheral axons.

title: Gamma motor neurons:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Gamma motor neurons:
options: Supply intrafusal fibres and keep the spindle sensitive
Supply extrafusal fibres and produce the force of contraction
body.explanation: Alpha-gamma coactivation keeps the spindle taut during contraction.

title: A toxin removes the inactivation gate of voltage-gated Na⁺ channels but leaves activation intact. The most likely effect on the action potential is
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A toxin removes the inactivation gate of voltage-gated Na⁺ channels but leaves activation intact. The most likely effect on the action potential is
options: A prolonged depolarization, because Na⁺ keeps entering
body.explanation: Inactivation is what stops Na⁺ entry and allows the falling phase; without it the membrane stays depolarized.

title: At rest, the membrane potential of a neuron (about -70 mV) lies closest to the equilibrium potential of
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: At rest, the membrane potential of a neuron (about -70 mV) lies closest to the equilibrium potential of
options: K⁺, because K⁺ leak channels are open
Na⁺, because the Na⁺/K⁺ pump moves 3 Na⁺ out
Ca²⁺, because Ca²⁺ is high outside
Cl⁻, because Cl⁻ is actively pumped in
Na⁺, because Na⁺ leak channels are open
body.explanation: At rest K⁺ permeability is high, so the potential sits near EK (about -90 mV); few Na⁺ channels are open.

title: Rubbing a bumped elbow relieves the pain. According to the gate control theory, this is because
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Rubbing a bumped elbow relieves the pain. According to the gate control theory, this is because
options: A-beta touch fibres activate inhibitory interneurons in the dorsal horn
The motor cortex blocks the thalamus
C fibres release more substance P
body.explanation: Large touch fibres (A-beta) and descending enkephalin neurons close the 'gate' on pain transmission in the dorsal horn.

title: Myosin II is a hexamer made of
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Myosin II is a hexamer made of
options: Two heavy chains and two light chains
Three heavy chains and three light chains
Four heavy chains and two light chains
Two heavy chains and four light chains
body.explanation: The head (S1) holds the ATP and actin binding sites; the neck is the lever arm.

title: Thanks to CSF buoyancy, the brain's effective weight falls from about 1400 g to about:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Thanks to CSF buoyancy, the brain's effective weight falls from about 1400 g to about:
body.explanation: Protection and buoyancy are major functions of CSF.

title: Saltatory conduction is possible because voltage-gated channels are concentrated at the
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Saltatory conduction is possible because voltage-gated channels are concentrated at the
body.explanation: Myelin (up to 300 layers) has no channels beneath it, so the signal jumps from node to node.

title: Nissl granules are absent from the
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Nissl granules are absent from the
body.explanation: Nissl granules (rough ER) are in the cell body and dendrites. That is why the axon cannot make protein.

title: A 22-year-old student shifts her gaze from a distant object to a book held 25 cm from her face. Which change keeps the text focused on the retina?
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: A 22-year-old student shifts her gaze from a distant object to a book held 25 cm from her face. Which change keeps the text focused on the retina?
options: Relaxation of the ciliary muscle and increased zonular tension
Contraction of the ciliary muscle and decreased zonular tension
Contraction of the ciliary muscle and flattening of the lens
Relaxation of the ciliary muscle and increased lens curvature
Contraction of the iris dilator muscle and increased lens curvature
body.explanation: The ciliary muscle contracts, zonules slacken and the lens rounds up. Near vision also brings convergence and miosis.

title: Neurons cannot divide because they lack:
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: Neurons cannot divide because they lack:
body.explanation: Every neuron has exactly one axon.

title: An inhibitory postsynaptic potential (IPSP) is typically produced by
subject: subj:physio

body.stem: An inhibitory postsynaptic potential (IPSP) is typically produced by
options: Entry of Cl⁻, which hyperpolarizes the membrane
Entry of Ca²⁺ into the presynaptic terminal
Entry of Na⁺, which depolarizes the membrane
body.explanation: EPSP: positive ions in (Na⁺), towards threshold. IPSP: negative ions in (Cl⁻), away from threshold.
